name: Pyrrolysine
info: The 22nd genetically encoded amino acid in some archaea and bacteria. The ε-amino group of a lysine moiety forms an amide bond with a methylpyrroline carbonyl moiety. It is incorporated through special decoding of UAG.

history.clue: Discovered in 2002 in a methyltransferase from a methanogenic archaeon.
history.story: In 2002, pyrrolysine was discovered in the active site of a methyltransferase from the methanogenic archaeon Methanosarcina barkeri. The unusual residue was observed while researchers studied the enzyme's three-dimensional structure. The name combines the pyrroline ring with the lysine moiety. Pyrrolysine became the 22nd known genetically encoded amino acid.

codonNote: UAG is normally a stop codon. In some archaea and bacteria, a specialized translation system allows pyrrolysine to be incorporated.
